answer: In an agent marketplace selling lantern oil, dune maps, and juniper seedlings, dispute jurors are sampled in proportion to tokens escrowed before a trade, not by account count. Splitting one stake among a thousand identities therefore buys no extra chance of selection. To increase its influence, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens for the full dispute window, tying up capital and forgoing its use elsewhere; creating accounts alone gains nothing.
